clue.text: Drop out of old American university

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone quits their studies at a long-established US college.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop something from a list is to leave it out, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Love I had, in part, for Baltimore singer

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the part 'had' the I 'in' it, so I goes inside the word for part

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A wistful line about a lost romance, mentioning a performer from Baltimore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baltimore singer' suggests a crooner from that city, but it is a bird: the Baltimore oriole, which also gives the city's baseball team its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltimore oriole is a North American songbird, so the bird is literally a singer named after Baltimore.

clue.text: Union leader, dramatic Irishman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Philip ..., a Union general in the American Civil War
second meaning: Richard Brinsley ..., the Irish playwright of The Rivals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Union leader' sounds like a trade-union boss; here it is a commander on the Union side in the Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to a famous Civil War cavalry general and to a celebrated Dublin-born playwright.

clue.text: Republican beset by pains in parts of feet

indicators.note: the Republican is surrounded by the pains, so R sits inside the word

parts.note: aches are pains

explanation.surface: A politician suffering from sore feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The arch is the curved section of the sole between heel and ball, a part of each foot.

clue.text: In non-U American way, help party with a supporter's badge

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: non-U means without U, and the American spelling of the word for a badge drops its U

parts.note: a favour is a rosette or ribbon worn to show support

explanation.surface: Phrased like etiquette advice on helping a party with a rosette, in an unrefined American style.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper-class; here it literally means 'without U', which is how American spelling differs from British.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone a favor is the idiom for helping them out, here in its US spelling.

clue.text: American space rocket, as sent up to go around

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to turn is to go around

explanation.surface: A US rocket is launched and circles the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn V was the NASA launch vehicle that carried the Apollo missions to the Moon.

clue.text: Founder of New York store with raincoat on display, finally

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat (short for mackintosh)

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of display

explanation.surface: A shop founder in Manhattan puts a raincoat in the window.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowland Hussey Macy founded the New York department store that still bears his name.

clue.text: US general giving computer to President

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
Chester Arthur was the 21st US President

explanation.surface: A general hands a computer to the head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas MacArthur commanded American forces in the Pacific in the Second World War.

clue.text: The young Clinton in part of New York or London

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the daughter of Bill and Hillary Clinton

definitions.text: part of New York or London
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a district of Manhattan, and also a district of west London

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to the Clintons' daughter and to neighbourhoods in both Manhattan and the Royal Borough of Kensington.

clue.text: American leader usually very cool — zero degrees

parts.note: zero is the letter O
BA and MA are university degrees

explanation.surface: A president's famous composure is described in terms of a temperature reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very cool — zero degrees' reads as a thermometer; zero gives O and the degrees are BA and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama, the 44th US President, was renowned for his calm temperament, nicknamed 'No-drama Obama'.

clue.text: Day for celebration, like the 7th of January, 8th of February, and 3rd of May

definitions.text: Day for celebration, like the 7th of January, 8th of February, and 3rd of May

parts.words: Day for celebration, like the 7th of January, 8th of February, and 3rd of May
parts.note: the listed dates are really letter positions: the 7th letter of January, the 8th of February and the 3rd of May are all Y, which is also a particular letter of the summer month's name

explanation.walkthrough: The dates look like a list of holidays, but they count letters: JANUARY's 7th, FEBRUARY's 8th and MAY's 3rd are each Y, just as Y is the fourth letter of JULY.
explanation.definitionFit: Independence Day in the United States, celebrated every year on that summer date.

clue.text: Deceive in LA, with dimes wrongly distributed

indicators.note: the letters of LA and dimes are handed out in the wrong order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A scam in Los Angeles where coins are handed out dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead is to lead someone into a false belief, the same as deceiving them.

clue.text: Male in charge introducing US blues, for example

indicators.note: the male in charge takes US into the middle, between M and IC

explanation.surface: A man in charge of a band brings the blues to America.
explanation.definitionFit: Blues is a genre, so it is an example of music.

clue.text: Drink, including regular American soft drink

indicators.note: the word for drink contains the word for regular

parts.note: to sup is to drink
even means regular, uniform

explanation.surface: A menu note that a beverage comes with a standard-issue fizzy pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' looks like the definition, but it is the outer part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven Up is a lemon-lime fizzy beverage brand from the United States.

clue.text: School exercises on TV channel bothersome for Americans

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise lessons at school
Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster

explanation.surface: Televised school gym lessons that Americans find irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is the UK's main satellite TV company; 'for Americans' says the answer is chiefly US usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is an informal US term for annoying or troublesome.

clue.text: Standard indications of rank in US army

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a standard is a flag, here the US flag

definitions.text: indications of rank in US army
definitions.meaning: second meaning: officers' rank insignia are stars and NCOs' are stripes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as an adjective meaning normal; it is the noun for a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the American flag, and also the stars and chevrons that mark military rank.

clue.text: Clearing vehicle in US currently parking without haste outside

indicators.note: the word for without haste goes outside the other two pieces

parts.note: slow means without haste
now means currently
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A slow-moving vehicle parked outside in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in US' marks the American spelling; British English has plough.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowplow is the vehicle that clears snow from roads, US spelling.

clue.text: Striking quality in US alien certainly spotted

indicators.note: spotted means the answer can be seen sitting within the words US alien certainly

explanation.surface: A sighting of an extraterrestrial in America with a remarkable feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Salience is prominence, the quality of standing out conspicuously.

clue.text: A spread organized for 11 events

indicators.note: the letters of a spread are organized into a new order

explanation.surface: A buffet laid out for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 refers to the answer at 11-across, the US national holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Street processions are a traditional feature of Independence Day celebrations across America.

clue.text: Harmony in town where fight for independence began

definitions.text: town where fight for independence began
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Massachusetts town where the first battles of the American Revolution were fought in 1775

explanation.definitionFit: The word means peaceful agreement, and is also the town that, with Lexington, saw the opening shots of the War of Independence.

clue.text: Reason for not gambling? Certainly not in America

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally having ..., so a dice game cannot be played
second meaning: the American slang phrase for 'no way'

explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase means lacking the cubes needed for craps; as US slang it is a flat refusal.

clue.text: People in party holding up in cowboy gear

indicators.note: the party members hold the reversed letters inside them

parts.note: Dems are Democrats, members of a US party

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters of in are read from the bottom, backwards

explanation.surface: Partygoers dressed as cowboys.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeans made of denim cloth are standard wear for cowboys.

clue.text: An unalienable right one's not bound to have

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the unalienable rights named in the Declaration of Independence
second meaning: freedom is what someone who is not tied up has

explanation.walkthrough: 'not bound to have' reads as 'not obliged to have'; it means 'not tied up'. The Declaration lists life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom from constraint is both a constitutional right and the state of not being bound.

clue.text: Dollar alien found in container

parts.note: a buck is slang for a dollar
ET is the extraterrestrial of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A dollar bill turns up together with an extraterrestrial in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is a container for carrying water.

clue.text: Sci-fi movie being celebrated now in US

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the holiday the puzzle marks, July 4th

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a blockbuster film about an alien attack and to America's national holiday.

clue.text: Some letters from Ohio, Washington, and another state

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a Midwestern US state, one beyond the two already named.

clue.text: American setting up king? No

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.walkthrough: Yank is informal for an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Yank is a colloquial term, mainly British, for any person from the United States.

clue.text: Crazy person finally back in Texan city

indicators.note: that letter goes in the middle of the city's name

parts.note: Waco is a city in Texas

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of back

explanation.surface: A madman eventually returns to his Texas hometown.
explanation.definitionFit: Wacko is informal slang for an eccentric or insane individual.

clue.text: Top US golfer demolished milk scone

indicators.note: the milk scone is demolished, its letters broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A star golfer wolfs down a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Phil Mickelson is a major-winning American professional on the golf tour.
